chunks: If the ruled fulfill the right of the ruler,
and the ruler fulfills their right, then right attains honor among them, the ways of religion become established, the signs of justice become balanced, and the sunnahs flow along their paths.
Thus time improves, the continuation of the state is hoped for, and the ambitions of the enemies are frustrated.
ai.seo_question: What are the mutual rights of the ruler and the ruled in Shia Islamic governance?
ai.summary: In this foundational text from the Letter to Malik al-Ashtar, Imam Ali defines the socio-political contract where the ruler's justice and the people's compliance create a stable state (dawla) rooted in divine law. This mutual fulfillment ensures that 'justice prevails' (azza al-haqq), a concept central to Shia political thought, leading to internal cohesion and external security against adversaries. The passage underscores that political legitimacy is contingent upon the practical implementation of religious ethics in governance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If the ruled fulfil the rights of the ruler and the ruler fulfils their rights, then right attains the position of honour among them, the ways of religion become established, signs of justice become fixed and the sunnah gains currency.
In this way time will improve, the continuance of government will be expected, and the aims of the enemies will be frustrated.
